security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan generates an illegal-instruction exception for WRS.NTO whenever (!isModeM && mstatus.TW), unconditionally — missing the spec-mandated misa.S gate. The spec PR operation() IDL explicitly requires CSR[misa].S == 1 as a prerequisite for the TW trap: 'if ((CSR[misa].S == 1) && (CSR[mstatus].TW == 1'b1)) { if (mode() != PrivilegeMode::M) { raise(IllegalInstruction) } }'. In XiangShan NewCSR.scala:1501, the condition is io.toDecode.illegalInst.wrs_nto := !isModeM && mstatus.regOut.TW, which fires the trap even when misa.S == 0 (S-mode not implemented). On an M+U-only configuration, a WRS.NTO with TW=1 in U-mode would incorrectly trap. Additionally, the spec explicitly gates the VTW trap on misa.H == 1; XiangShan uses privState.V as a proxy for H-extension presence (equivalent in practice since V cannot be 1 without H), so no divergence there. Note: this is primarily a latent spec-compliance gap since XiangShan's production configs always have misa.S = 1.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: Grep for 'illegalInst.wrs_nto' in NewCSR.scala — the expression must include a misa.S gate term (e.g., 'misa.rdata.S &&') before the TW check; currently absent. Similarly verify the VTW virtual-instruction trap at line 1502 has an explicit misa.H gate rather than relying solely on privState.V as a proxy.
security_spec.summary: WRS.NTO illegal-instruction TW trap is not gated on misa.S per spec PR #1669; on M+U-only configs TW=1 would incorrectly trap WRS.NTO despite TW being an S-mode concept with no S-mode present
